defs.def: to expect sth 预料；预期

ex.s: Always make your presentation just a bit shorter than anticipated.
ex.t: 让听众意犹未尽比让他们在座位上不安地扭动、等待演讲结束要好。

ex.s: However, they did not anticipate seeing such an open country, and were truly amazed.
ex.t: 然而，他们并没有预料到会看到如此开阔的乡村，因而感到十分惊讶。

ex.s: They realise that ESCAPE itdoes notmatterhowattractivetheidealinked with the product is - most people know and to Paradise anticipate that the main purpose of the advertisement istomakecustomersbuythe product.
ex.t: 他们意识到，与产品相关的那个诱人理念其实并不重要——大多数人都心知肚明，并且都能预料到，广告的主要目的就是让顾客购买产品。

defs.def: to see what might happen in the future and take action to prepare for it 预见，预计（并做准备）

ex.s: Twenty years ago, positions in social technologies or energy efficiency did not even exist, and it is difficult to anticipate the new positions which will emerge twenty years from now.
ex.t: 二十年前，社交媒体或能源效率方面的职位甚至还不存在，很难预见二十年后会出现哪些新职位。

ex.s: Leon graduated after demonstrating the appropriate level of understanding and technical competence, (6) he now anticipates a long and happy career as an electrician.
ex.t: 莱昂在展现出相应的理解水平和技术能力后毕业了，（6）他现在期待着作为一名电工拥有漫长而愉快的职业前程。

defs.def: to think with pleasure and excitement about sth that is going to happen 期盼；期望
to do sth before it can be done by sb else 先于 … 做；早于 … 行动

ex.s: As Morrie says, “Once you learn how to die, you learn how to live.” As Morrie anticipates his own death, he observes everything as though through new eyes－the things around him seem more beautiful than ever before and hold new meanings.
ex.t: 正如莫里所说：“一旦你学会了如何面对死亡，你就学会了如何生活。”当莫里预感到自己的死亡时，他以全新的眼光观察一切——周围的事物似乎比以往任何时候都更美，也更具新的意义。
